You only need enough answered responses to fill the requested number of clusters; if there are too few, the call returns ``400`` (lower ``n_clusters`` or wait for more responses). tools.name: studies_embed_get-snippet
tools.description: Generate the HTML install snippet for embedding this study's interview widget. Pass ``publishable_key`` (from key creation) to fill it into the snippet; otherwise a placeholder is emitted. ``mode`` selects the widget presentation (default ``chat``). The signed-token variant is also returned for servers that mint per-visitor JWS (HS256) tokens with the key's signing secret. **Metadata.** Both snippets can carry context that is stored with the interview and shown alongside the transcript (plan, tenant, seat count, and so on). The basic snippet includes a ``data-metadata`` placeholder holding an example flat JSON object — replace its keys with your own, or delete the attribute if you have no context to attach. * ``data-metadata`` is **page-supplied and therefore untrusted**: a visitor can change it with browser dev tools before the interview starts. That is fine for context you only want to read next to the transcript. It is not fine when the interview has to act on the value — asking enterprise-only questions, skipping a section for trial users, or reporting results split by plan. * For those cases use ``signed_snippet`` instead of the basic one: your server mints a short-lived token (HS256, ``kid`` header = the publishable key, ``sub`` = your stable end-user id, ``exp`` no more than 900s after ``iat``) with a ``metadata`` claim, signed with that key's signing secret, and the page sends it as ``data-signed-token`` in place of ``data-publishable-key``. Those values are recorded with provenance ``'token'`` (shown as verified in the dashboard) and override any page-supplied value of the same name, so a tag may carry ``data-metadata`` as well when some values need not be verified. * ``participant_id`` is the one key with a meaning of its own: whatever value it holds is also stored on the interview as ``external_participant_id``, so an embedded study can be joined back to your own users the same way a link built with ``?participant_id=`` can. It stays in the metadata bag as well. Page-supplied it is no more trustworthy than any other key — it labels the row and identifies nobody; send it in the signed token when it has to be verified. Keep it pseudonymous either way (a hash of your user id, not an email): it is stored on the interview, exported, and sent on the ``interview.completed`` webhook. * Limits, enforced at bootstrap — a payload that breaks any of them is rejected outright, so validate before you send: at most 32 keys; key names match ``^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$``; scalar values only (string <= 1 KB, number, bool, null) — no nested objects or arrays; total serialized size <= the key's ``metadata_max_bytes``. Required: study_id. Optional: publishable_key, mode (default: chat). Returns the EmbedSnippetOut.

params.name: publishable_key
params.description: Publishable key to embed in the snippet

tools.name: studies_graph_activate
tools.description: Switch the study to `graph` mode: interviews follow the stored flow instead of the linear question list. Requires a flow that last saved without problems. The question list is left untouched — `deactivate_graph` switches back to it at any time. Required: study_id. Returns the new GraphModeOut.

tools.name: studies_graph_check
tools.description: Validate a flow and report every problem, changing nothing. Use this while drafting: iterate here until `valid` is true, then save with `set_graph`. Pass the flow in `flow`, or omit it to re-check the study's stored flow. Each problem names the step it is on using **your own step ids**, a stable `code`, and a plain-language `message`. Common codes: * `no_default` — a decision step has several paths but no `'default': true` one * `unreachable` / `no_path_to_end` — a step can't be reached, or can't reach an end * `var_not_guaranteed` — a step uses a captured answer that earlier branching means might not exist yet * `unattached` — an extract/webhook/context_fetch step is missing `after`/`before` * `missing_max_revisits` — a step inside a loop has no repeat limit * `private_url` — a fetch or webhook URL points at an internal address When the flow is valid, `compiled` shows the derived captured-answer table and the final execution order with side steps spliced into place — worth checking that attachments landed where you intended. Required: study_id. Optional: flow. Returns array of FlowCheckError.

params.name: flow
params.description: The flow to check. Omit to re-check the study's stored flow.

tools.name: studies_graph_deactivate
tools.description: Switch the study back to `linear` mode. The stored flow is kept, just not used. Required: study_id. Returns the new GraphModeOut.

tools.name: studies_graph_get
tools.description: The study's interview flow, in the same shape `set_graph` accepts — so you can read it, change part of it, and write it back. Also reports whether the flow is the study's active interview script (`interview_mode`), and its `graph_version`, which you can pass to `set_graph` or `patch_graph` to avoid overwriting an edit made in the browser meanwhile. `flow` is null when the study has no interview flow yet; it still runs its linear question list, and `import_questions_to_graph` will turn that list into a starting flow. Required: study_id. Returns array of FlowCheckError.

tools.name: studies_graph_get-flow-signals
tools.description: The delivery config behind every 'Send a signal' (`webhook`) step in the saved flow, **including the signing secret** each step's deliveries are signed with. A signal is fired by the interviewer mid-interview, at the point in the flow where the step sits — distinct from the organization-level webhooks (the Webhooks endpoints), which this dashboard fires for lifecycle events like `interview.completed`. The secret is minted the first time the step is saved and kept stable across later saves, so a receiver configured once keeps verifying. Verify each delivery's `webhook-signature` against the secret for the step that sent it before acting on the body, and dedupe on `webhook-id`. To see what a particular interview actually sent, and whether it was accepted, use `get_interview_fetches_and_signals`. Required: study_id. Returns array of FlowSignalOut.

tools.name: studies_graph_import-questions-to
tools.description: Build a straight-line flow from the study's existing linear questions — start → each question in order → end — and save it, **replacing any flow the study already has**. The usual starting point: you get a flow that behaves exactly like the current interview, then add branching to it with `patch_graph`. Each question captures its answer as `q1`, `q2`, … so you can branch on them or pipe them into later question text straight away. Does not change the study's interview mode; call `activate_graph` when ready. Required: study_id. Returns array of FlowCheckError.

tools.name: studies_graph_patch
tools.description: Apply targeted edits to the stored flow instead of rewriting it — safer than read-modify-write on a large flow, and it leaves untouched steps exactly as the researcher arranged them. Operations are applied in order to the stored flow, then the **result is validated as a whole**, so passing through an invalid intermediate state is fine. As with `set_graph`, nothing is saved unless the end state is valid. * `{'op': 'add_node', 'node': {...}}` * `{'op': 'update_node', 'id': 'q_pets', 'config': {'text': 'New wording?'}}` — merges into the step's config; omitted keys keep their value, `null` clears one * `{'op': 'remove_node', 'id': 'q_pets'}` — also drops its connections and detaches anything attached to it * `{'op': 'add_edge', 'edge': {'from': 'branch', 'to': 'q_ideal', 'default': true}}` * `{'op': 'update_edge', 'from': 'branch', 'to': 'q_story', 'condition': {...}}` * `{'op': 'remove_edge', 'from': 'branch', 'to': 'q_story'}` Example — rewording a question and raising its turn limit: ```json {'ops': [{'op': 'update_node', 'id': 'q_story', 'config': {'text': 'Tell me more about your pet.', 'max_turns': 6}}]} ```. Required: study_id, ops. Optional: expected_graph_version. Returns array of FlowCheckError.

params.name: ops
params.description: Edits applied in order to the stored flow, then validated as a whole.

tools.name: studies_graph_set
tools.description: Write a complete interview flow, replacing whatever is stored. **Nothing is saved unless the flow is valid** — on any problem this returns 422 with the same error list `check_graph` gives, and the stored flow is untouched. Steps are connected two different ways, and mixing them up is the most common mistake: * `start`, `end`, `question` and `decision` steps sit on the interview's path and are connected with `edges`. * `extract` and `webhook` steps attach to a question with `'after': '<question id>'`, and `context_fetch` attaches with `'before': '<question id>'`. They are never listed in `edges`; the compiler splices them into the right place. A minimal branching flow: ```json {'flow': {'nodes': [ {'id': 'start', 'type': 'start'}, {'id': 'q_pets', 'type': 'question', 'config': {'qtype': 'options', 'text': 'Do you have pets?', 'options': ['Yes', 'No'], 'output_var': 'has_pets'}}, {'id': 'branch', 'type': 'decision', 'config': {'mode': 'deterministic'}}, {'id': 'q_story', 'type': 'question', 'config': {'qtype': 'open_ended', 'text': 'Tell me about your pet.'}}, {'id': 'q_ideal', 'type': 'question', 'config': {'qtype': 'open_ended', 'text': 'Describe your ideal pet.'}}, {'id': 'end', 'type': 'end'} ], 'edges': [ {'from': 'start', 'to': 'q_pets'}, {'from': 'q_pets', 'to': 'branch'}, {'from': 'branch', 'to': 'q_story', 'condition': {'var': 'has_pets', 'op': 'eq', 'value': 'Yes'}, 'priority': 0}, {'from': 'branch', 'to': 'q_ideal', 'default': true, 'priority': 1}, {'from': 'q_story', 'to': 'end'}, {'from': 'q_ideal', 'to': 'end'} ]}} ``` Use `{{captured_answer}}` in question text to pipe an earlier answer in. The validator enforces that a captured answer is only used where it is guaranteed to exist. Saving does not switch the study into graph mode — call `activate_graph` for that. The flow is fully editable afterwards in the browser flow editor, and step ids, positions and webhook signing secrets survive round trips. Required: study_id, flow. Optional: expected_graph_version.

params.name: expected_graph_version
params.description: Optimistic concurrency: pass the `graph_version` you last read and the write is refused with 409 if a researcher has since edited the flow in the browser. Omit to overwrite unconditionally.

params.name: flow-edges
params.description: Connections between start/end/question/decision steps only. extract, webhook and context_fetch steps attach with `after`/`before` instead.

params.name: flow-nodes
params.description: Every step in the flow. Exactly one `start`, at least one `end`.

tools.name: studies_interviews_find-by-external-id
tools.description: Every interview in this study that arrived carrying ``external_participant_id`` — your own id for the person, from the entry link's ``?participant_id=`` or the embed metadata bag's ``participant_id`` key — in full detail, newest first. The direct answer to 'did this person finish, and what happened?' when you hold your id for them and not ours. Expect more than one row sometimes: a person who abandons and starts again has an interview per attempt, and ``total`` says how many. An empty list means nobody has arrived on a link carrying that id — not that they were screened out. For the transcripts behind these interviews, pass the same id to ``bulk_transcripts``; for one interview's messages, ``get_transcript`` with the id from a row here. The match is exact, and the id is participant-supplied text: it says which of your own records to look at, it does not authenticate anybody. Required: study_id, external_participant_id. tools.name: studies_questions_validate
tools.description: Review the study's questions before it goes live, the same check the dashboard's **Validate** button runs. Returns three things: * **Ethics** — one pass/fail for the whole set, with the specific concerns when it fails (offensive or intrusive wording, targeting under-13s, asking for identifying, financial, or medical details, requesting explicit images). * **Language quality** — per question, any clarity, grammar, or spelling problem, judged in the study's own language. * **Redundancy** — per question, which other questions it overlaps with and how. Findings carry both the question's ``number`` (1-based interview order) and its ``question_id``, so you can act on them with ``PATCH .../questions/{question_id}``. Nothing is changed by this call, and no result is stored — it is advisory only. This is a model call over the whole question set, so it typically takes ten to twenty seconds. Required: study_id.

tools.name: studies_recruitment_get
tools.description: Participation links, quota status, and pre-interview gate flags. The links come back bare: append ``&source=<your campaign tag>`` and/or ``&participant_id=<your id for this person>`` to attribute the arrival — they are recorded on the interview as ``web_source`` and ``external_participant_id``, and can be read back and filtered on. ``participant_id`` here is your own free-text id, not the Deutero participant UUID of the same name. Required: study_id. Returns the RecruitmentOut.

tools.name: studies_recruitment_update
tools.description: Set a custom short-link slug, the response quota, and/or the post-completion redirect URL. Omitted fields are untouched; set ``clear_max_responses`` to true to remove the quota. The slug must be unique across all studies. The redirect URL may carry ``{{external_participant_id}}``, which is replaced at the end of the interview with the id that interview arrived with (from the link's ``?participant_id=`` or the embed metadata bag) — the usual way to hand a panel or CRM its own id back on completion. It expands to the empty string for an interview that carried no id, so a callback that requires one should be built from links that always set it. ``{{external_participant_id}}`` is the only placeholder either redirect understands. A single-braced ``{external_participant_id}`` is corrected to it (a URL stored with the literal text would silently never substitute); any other ``{{…}}`` is stored untouched but named in ``redirect_url_warning``, which is null when the URL was stored exactly as sent. Required: study_id. Optional: clear_max_responses (default: false), max_responses, redirect_url (plus 1 more). Returns the updated RecruitmentOut.

params.name: clear_max_responses
params.description: Set true to remove the response quota

params.name: max_responses
params.description: Response quota; set to null via clear_max_responses

params.name: redirect_url
params.description: Post-completion redirect. Use {{external_participant_id}} anywhere in it to hand your own participant id back to a panel or CRM — e.g. https://panel.example/done?pid={{external_participant_id}}

params.name: short_url_slug
params.description: Custom short-link slug (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Must be unique across all studies.

tools.name: studies_screening_create
tools.description: Appends a multiple-choice qualifying question. ``acceptable_options`` must be a subset of ``options``. Required: study_id, acceptable_options, options, question. Returns the new ScreeningQuestionOut.

params.name: acceptable_options
params.description: Subset of options that qualify the participant

tools.name: studies_screening_delete
tools.description: Removes the question and renumbers the remaining list. Any recorded participant answers to it are deleted with it. Required: question_id, study_id. Returns the SuccessResponse. Destructive.

tools.name: studies_screening_get
tools.description: Settings plus the ordered screening question list. Required: study_id. Returns array of ScreeningQuestionOut.

tools.name: studies_screening_reorder-questions
tools.description: Supply every screening question ID in the desired order. Required: study_id, question_ids. Returns array of ScreeningQuestionOut.

params.name: question_ids
params.description: All question IDs in the desired order

tools.name: studies_screening_set-settings
tools.description: Enable/disable screening and set the disqualification message and redirect URL. Disabling preserves questions and settings. The redirect URL may carry ``{{external_participant_id}}``, replaced at screen-out time with the id this interview arrived with, so a panel callback can say who bounced as well as who finished. It is the only placeholder understood: a single-braced ``{external_participant_id}`` is corrected to it, and any other ``{{…}}`` is stored untouched but named in ``redirect_url_warning``. Required: study_id, enabled. Optional: disqualification_message, redirect_url. Returns the updated ScreeningSettingsOut.

params.name: disqualification_message
params.description: Message shown to participants who do not qualify

params.name: enabled
params.description: Whether screening runs before the interview

params.name: redirect_url
params.description: Optional URL disqualified participants are sent to. Takes the same placeholder as the completion redirect: {{external_participant_id}} is replaced with the id this interview arrived with (the entry link's ?participant_id=, or the embed metadata bag's participant_id key), so a panel can be told who was screened out as well as who finished. It expands to the empty string for an interview that carried no id

tools.name: studies_screening_update
tools.description: Update a screening question. Required: question_id, study_id. Optional: acceptable_options, options, question. Returns the updated ScreeningQuestionOut.

tools.name: studies_search_transcripts
tools.description: Search participant answers in a study. * ``mode=string`` — full-text (websearch syntax: quoted phrases, ``-term``) fused with trigram fuzzy matching. No external services required. * ``mode=semantic`` — embedding similarity over stored response vectors (query embedded with Voyage AI). Finds conceptual matches that share no words with the query. Only messages that have embeddings are searchable. * ``mode=hybrid`` (default) — reciprocal-rank fusion of all three rankings; falls back to string-only behavior if semantic search is unavailable and ``strict`` is false. Optionally scope to one question with ``question_id`` (questions-table ID, or graph node ID for graph-mode studies). Required: study_id, q. Optional: mode (default: hybrid), question_id, completed_only (default: false) (plus 4 more). Returns array of SearchHit.

params.name: question_id
params.description: Restrict to one question. A questions-table id for a linear study, or a graph step id for a flow study — the step id you authored, exactly as ``get_graph`` reports it

params.name: external_participant_id
params.description: Restrict to the interviews of one person, named by your own id for them (the entry link's ?participant_id= or the embed metadata bag's participant_id key)

params.name: strict
params.description: hybrid mode: fail (503) instead of silently degrading to string search when semantic search is unavailable

tools.name: studies_simulations_list
tools.description: Every simulation run for the study, newest first, with the interview each produced and what it cost. Required: study_id. Optional: status, limit (default: 50), offset (default: 0). Returns array of SimulationOut.

tools.name: studies_simulations_run
tools.description: Start one simulated interview and return immediately — the run continues in the background, so poll ``GET /simulations/{simulation_id}`` for its outcome. Credits are reserved at the estimated cost before the run starts; a request that would exceed the balance is refused with 402 and costs nothing. Plan limits apply: simulations are not available on Hobby, and the standard/premium tiers need Solo/Team. Run one persona per call; to sweep a panel, call once per persona. Required: study_id. Optional: deliver_signals (default: false), model_tier (default: open_weights), persona (plus 1 more). Returns the new SimulationStartOut.

params.name: deliver_signals
params.description: Let this run's 'Send a signal' steps reach their real endpoints. Off by default: a simulation records what each signal would have sent without sending it. When on, receivers get exactly what a live interview sends, plus an X-Deutero-Simulated header.

params.name: model_tier
params.description: Which model conducts and answers the interview: 'open_weights' (cheapest), 'standard' (Solo plan and up), or 'premium' (Team plan). Higher tiers cost more credits per run. The former name 'frontier' is still accepted and means 'premium'.

params.name: persona
params.description: Ad-hoc persona description, used when no ``persona_id`` is given. Overrides the stored text if both are supplied.

params.name: persona_id
params.description: Persona to play the participant. Omit to run against a generic participant, or pass ``persona`` to use ad-hoc text instead.

tools.name: studies_stats_get-study
tools.description: Counts of started/completed/incomplete interviews, completion rate, and quota fill relative to ``max_responses``. Simulated (persona) interviews are counted separately. Required: study_id. Returns the StudyStatsOut.

tools.name: studies_transcripts_bulk
tools.description: Full transcripts for a study's interviews, newest interview first, paginated by interview. Each transcript also carries ``variables`` — the answers that interview captured into Interview Flow variables, empty for a study that captures nothing. Filter with ``completed`` and ``include_simulated``. For a single interview use ``GET /interviews/{interview_id}/transcript``. Pass ``external_participant_id`` to fetch the transcripts of one person by your own id for them — the id the entry link's ``?participant_id=`` or the embed metadata bag carried. Each transcript carries that id back, so an export can be joined to your own records without a second call. Required: study_id. Optional: completed, include_simulated (default: false), external_participant_id (plus 2 more). Returns array of InterviewTranscript.

params.name: external_participant_id
params.description: Only interviews that arrived with this exact id — your own identifier for the participant. The way to fetch one person's transcript when you hold your id for them and not ours

tools.name: studies_welcome_delete
tools.description: Delete a translation. Required: translation_id, study_id. Returns the SuccessResponse. Destructive.

tools.name: studies_welcome_get
tools.description: Get the welcome message. Required: study_id. Returns the WelcomeOut.

tools.name: studies_welcome_list-translations
tools.description: List welcome-message translations. Required: study_id. Returns array of WelcomeTranslationOut.

tools.name: studies_welcome_set
tools.description: Create or replace the study's welcome/consent message. Set ``consent`` to true to require participants to explicitly agree before the interview begins. Required: study_id, message. Optional: consent (default: false). Returns the updated WelcomeOut.

params.name: consent
params.description: Whether the participant must explicitly consent to proceed

params.name: message
params.description: Welcome/consent message shown before the interview

tools.name: studies_welcome_upsert-translation
tools.description: Upserts the translation for ``target_language`` (one translation per target language). The welcome message must be set first. Required: study_id, target_language, translation_text. Optional: source_language (default: English). Returns the updated WelcomeTranslationOut.

params.name: source_language
params.description: Source language name or ISO code

params.name: target_language
params.description: Target language name or ISO code (e.g. 'Spanish' or 'es')

tools.name: webhooks_create
tools.description: Subscribe a URL of yours to organization events. The response carries the **signing secret, the only time it is ever shown** — store it before doing anything else, and verify every delivery against it. The endpoint receives events for every study the organization owns. Name the events you want in ``events``; an empty list means all of them. Required: label, url. Optional: enabled (default: true), events (default: []). Returns the new WebhookCreatedOut.

params.name: events
params.description: Event types to subscribe to. **An empty list subscribes to every event** — pass the ones you want to narrow it. Unknown names are dropped; call list_webhook_event_types for the catalogue.

params.name: label
params.description: How you will recognize this endpoint in the list

params.name: url
params.description: Publicly reachable http(s) URL that receives the POSTs

tools.name: webhooks_delete
tools.description: Permanently removes the endpoint and its delivery log. To stop deliveries temporarily, set ``enabled`` false with update_webhook instead — deleting throws the signing secret away with the endpoint. Required: webhook_id. Returns the WebhookDeleteOut. Destructive.

tools.name: webhooks_list
tools.description: Every webhook endpoint in your organization, newest first. Signing secrets are not included — they are shown only when an endpoint is created or its secret is rotated. Returns the WebhookListOut.

tools.name: webhooks_list-event-types
tools.description: Every event an endpoint can subscribe to, what makes it fire, and the fields its payload carries — read this before creating an endpoint, so the subscription names events that exist and the receiver knows what it will get. ``interview.completed`` and ``interview.started`` carry ``external_participant_id``, your own id for the participant, which is what lets a receiver act on a finished interview without calling back. Returns the WebhookEventTypeListOut.

tools.name: webhooks_update
tools.description: Partial update: only the fields you send change. Set ``enabled`` false to pause deliveries without losing the endpoint or its secret. Changing ``events`` replaces the subscription list rather than adding to it. Required: webhook_id. Optional: enabled, events, label (plus 1 more). Returns array of string.

params.name: enabled
params.description: false pauses deliveries without deleting the endpoint

params.name: events
params.description: Event types to subscribe to. **An empty list subscribes to every event** — pass the ones you want to narrow it. Unknown names are dropped; call list_webhook_event_types for the catalogue.

tools.name: webhooks_deliveries_list-webhook
tools.description: The delivery log for one endpoint, newest first: what was sent, who it was about, the status your server returned, and the error if it failed. This is the record to read when an expected event never arrived — a 4xx or a connection error here says the delivery was attempted and your receiver refused it, while no row at all says nothing fired (check that the endpoint is enabled and subscribed to that event type). Interview deliveries carry external_participant_id, your own id for the participant, so this log reconciles against your own records: success=false lists the people you were told about but may never have acted on, and external_participant_id=<id> shows every attempt for one person. Deliveries logged before that field existed report null. Required: webhook_id. Optional: event_type, success, external_participant_id (plus 2 more). Returns array of WebhookDeliveryOut.

params.name: event_type
params.description: Only deliveries of this event type

params.name: success
params.description: true = only successes, false = only failures

params.name: external_participant_id
params.description: Only deliveries carrying this participant id of yours. Combine with success=false to answer 'was this person ever successfully notified?' without pulling the whole log.

tools.name: webhooks_rotate-secret_rotate-webhook-secret
tools.description: Mint a new signing secret for this endpoint and return it — the only other time a secret is shown. **The previous secret stops verifying immediately**, so deploy the new one to your receiver before the next event fires, or expect signature failures in between. Use this when the secret from ``create_webhook`` was lost or leaked. Required: webhook_id. Returns the new WebhookSecretOut.

novel_features.name: Flow behavior coverage
novel_features.description: Shows how an Interview Flow actually routed across a whole study: every branch arm's share, how often the otherwise path fired, classifier errors, which steps interviews reached, and which declared variables are being captured. Flow-mode studies only: a linear study has no branch or flow records and correctly returns nothing.

novel_features.name: Payout reconciliation
novel_features.description: Finds participants who completed a study but were never successfully notified, by joining completed interviews against the webhook deliveries that were supposed to tell your system about them.

novel_features.name: Study definition diff
novel_features.description: Compares two complete study definitions field by field — details, welcome and translations, screening, characteristics, questions or flow, recruitment — or compares a live study against a saved bundle file.

novel_features.name: Answer rectangle
novel_features.description: Turns a study into a real table: one row per interview, one column per question or captured variable, with the external participant id as the join key and optional participant characteristic columns via --with-characteristics. Works for both linear and flow studies.

novel_features.name: Flow effects audit
novel_features.description: Aggregates what a flow's side steps actually did across a study: failed data fetches with status codes, undelivered signals, and dry-run signals from simulations kept separate from real ones. Flow-mode studies only: a linear study has no branch or flow records and correctly returns nothing.

novel_features.name: Study bundle export and apply
novel_features.description: Snapshots an entire study definition — details, welcome and translations, screening, characteristics, questions or flow, recruitment — into one file. The write half is a separate command, 'study apply --file <f>', which plans by default and writes only with --confirm, and which replays whole-resource sections only (question lists replay via 'studies questions').

novel_features.name: Rehearsal vs reality diff
novel_features.description: Compares the simulated persona cohort against real participants on the same measures: step reach, branch arm mix, variable capture rate, message count and duration. Needs both cohorts; branch and variable measures are flow-mode only.

novel_features.name: Fielding burn rate
novel_features.description: Completions per day against the response quota, projecting the date the quota fills.

novel_features.name: Cross-tab
novel_features.description: Segments any scale or options question by any participant characteristic, with per-cell counts and per-segment completion rate.

novel_features.name: Saturation curve
novel_features.description: Counts how many genuinely new terms each successive interview contributes, and marks the point where the curve flattens. A mechanical word-level proxy for new content, not a judgement about meaning.
